arguments.summary: Policy transmission is most direct for NVDA: its FY27 Q3 outlook assumes no China Data Center compute revenue, while its filing describes effective foreclosure from China, license uncertainty and Taiwan/South Korea supply reliance. MU’s supplied filing instead supports an unquantified tariff/trade-investigation and manufacturing-regulation channel. QQQ has dated look-through exposure to both issuers, so these channels can transmit to the fund but cannot be converted into a fund loss estimate.

claims.text: The January 15, 2026 BIS final rule changed review to case-by-case, rather than presumed denial, only for qualifying advanced-computing commodities exported from the United States to China or Macau, subject to technical thresholds and extensive supply, shipment-cap, end-user/KYC and U.S. third-party-testing conditions; it did not establish approval or general market access.

NVIDIA’s disclosed Q3 FY27 outlook assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. Its August filing also states it is effectively foreclosed from the China market by U.S. export controls, identifies uncertain and potentially burdensome licensing, and says China has discouraged purchase/import/use of its data-center products, including China-specific compliant products.

For the next 63 sessions, further tightening or adverse license/customer treatment would principally threaten NVDA through lost optional China revenue, customer substitution and support friction—not deterioration of China Data Center revenue embedded in the disclosed Q3 outlook. Conversely, a qualifying license approval could restore optionality, but neither the rule nor disclosure establishes approval, product eligibility, customer eligibility, volume or financial benefit.

NVDA downside scenario: a new restriction, license denial/delay, or Chinese implementation that prevents customer use of permitted products would reinforce China foreclosure and could also impair customer relationships; an observable reversal would be a BIS rule/license decision plus NVIDIA disclosure that China Data Center revenue is included in outlook. Separately, any disruption/restriction affecting component, part or service supply from Taiwan or South Korea would impair supply, as disclosed.

Micron’s June 2026 filing says the scope and outcome of the BIS Section 232 semiconductor-import investigation and subsequently announced Section 301 investigations were unknown; either could lead to tariffs or trade restrictions. Micron states that resulting mitigation could add costs, manufacturing delays or other difficulties, and that manufacturing is subject to laws and regulations in numerous jurisdictions.

MU downside scenario: an eventual tariff/trade measure that raises input or selling costs, disrupts manufacturing, or weakens customers’ end demand could pressure its AI-memory demand and margin assumptions. The discriminator is an enacted measure with defined product/country coverage and Micron disclosure of affected materials, manufacturing, customers or quantified cost—not merely the existence of an investigation.

QQQ’s sponsor-reported equity holdings effective September 19, 2026 show NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%; the published equity view excludes certain cash/derivative positions and has an unknown-weight position. These are dated fund weights, not current holdings or a policy-loss estimate.

A policy shock specific to NVDA or MU has a dated transmission channel to QQQ through these constituent weights, while QQQ diversifies issuer-specific exposure across its reported holdings. The comparative magnitude of the fund effect is unknown because policy sensitivity of both holdings and the remainder of the fund is unquantified.

gaps.description: Current legal status after the January 15 rule—including amendments, current licensing practice and any issuer-specific approvals—is not verified. This limits only assertions of current eligibility or quantified NVDA impact; the dated-rule and conditional-transmission analysis remain usable.

Supplied disclosures do not quantify NVDA China revenue, license pipeline, product eligibility, Taiwan/South Korea supply concentration, or the financial effect of a disruption. No loss coefficient or preference conclusion should be inferred from these channels.

No supplied primary policy text or issuer disclosure identifies a specific enacted trade measure, affected geography/product/customer, or quantified financial exposure for MU. The investigation-based scenario is conditional only.
QQQ holdings are dated and do not establish current weights, constituent policy sensitivity, or ETF-level policy impact.

assumptions: The January 15, 2026 Federal Register text is treated as valid dated legal text, not certification of the regime as of the evaluation cutoff.
Policy analysis does not alter the supplied company EPS/multiple sensitivities; no policy loss percentage is assumed.
A later rule, license decision or issuer disclosure during the 63-session horizon can change operational assumptions without proving a price response.
arguments.counter_thesis: NVDA’s disclosed guidance already excludes China Data Center compute revenue, which may reduce immediate exposure to further China-access deterioration; license relaxation could be upside. MU’s broad trade-risk disclosure may prove immaterial if no adverse measure is enacted or costs are mitigated. QQQ’s diversified composition may dilute either issuer-specific shock. None of these offsets is quantified in the supplied evidence.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA’s policy/business assumption if BIS issues an amendment or a license decision, or NVIDIA states that China Data Center compute revenue is included in (or excluded from) updated outlook: confirmed permitted sales would add optionality; a denial/new restriction or continued exclusion would sustain the foreclosure assumption.

Review MU’s downside assumption if a Section 232/301 measure is enacted with defined semiconductor/material/product coverage or Micron identifies affected sourcing, manufacturing, customers or costs: this would replace the current investigation-only conditional scenario.

Review QQQ policy transmission if the sponsor publishes revised holdings after a material NVDA/MU policy event: changed constituent weights alter the dated look-through channel, but do not by themselves quantify fund impact.

shared_exposures.mechanism: China advanced-computing export controls and license decisions can affect NVDA sales optionality and hence QQQ through its dated NVDA holding.
shared_exposures.qualification: QQQ weight is dated; neither NVDA exposure amount nor ETF impact is quantified.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Potential semiconductor tariff/trade restrictions can affect MU costs, manufacturing or customer demand and hence transmit to QQQ through its dated MU holding.
shared_exposures.qualification: No enacted measure or MU loss amount is established; QQQ fund impact is unknown.
